jurisdiction.name: Zimbabwe
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Zimbabwe's only binding AI-relevant rules are the automated-decision provisions of the Cyber and Data Protection Act and its 2024 licensing regulations, which bar solely automated decisions with legal effects and automated decisions on children's data, enforced by the telecoms regulator POTRAZ as Data Protection Authority. POTRAZ also published a 2023 assessment of AI in the postal and telecommunications sector. The ICT ministry has posted a National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026-2030, which promises a future AI law, an AI ethics board and a regulatory sandbox, but the document gives no publication date, so it is tracked as a lead.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Information Communication Technology, Postal and Courier Services
Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority of Zimbabwe (POTRAZ)
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents read in full on the ICT ministry's and POTRAZ's websites. The National AI Strategy 2026-2030 is on the ministry's website but states no publication date and no official launch notice was found, so it is tracked as a lead until it can be dated from an official source. Parliament's and the central bank's websites could not be accessed, so pending bills and any central bank AI guidelines could not be checked.

instruments.english_title: Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] (Act No. 5 of 2021)
instruments.current_status: In force since 3 December 2021 (date of commencement stated in the consolidated text). Enacted as Act No. 5 of 2021 (originally headed Data Protection Act); re-gazetted with its new title on 11 March 2022 per the Law Reviser's note. POTRAZ also publishes the 2021 Act as gazetted (Data-Protection-Act-5-of-2021.pdf) and the Ministry of ICT links a copy. Implemented by S.I. 155 of 2024; POTRAZ opened a consultation in October 2026 on administrative penalties (see leads).
instruments.summary: Zimbabwe's data protection and cybersecurity law, which designates POTRAZ as the Data Protection Authority, establishes a Cyber Security Centre and sets rules for processing personal data wholly or partly by automated means. Section 25 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, unless they consented or the decision is based on law; section 20 requires controllers to notify the Authority before automated processing operations. It also amends the Criminal Law Code on cyber-crime and electronic evidence.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only binding Zimbabwean law with explicit rules on automated decision-making and profiling; governs data used to train and run AI systems.

instruments.current_status: In force (gazetted 2024). The scanned gazette copy on the POTRAZ site states S.I. 155 of 2024 but not the gazette day, so only the year is recorded. In October 2026 POTRAZ published a consultation paper and draft amendment regulations introducing administrative penalties (see leads).
instruments.summary: Statutory Instrument 155 of 2024, made by the ICT Minister under section 32 of the Cyber and Data Protection Act, introduces licensing of data controllers, data protection officer appointments, security and breach-notification rules. Section 10(3) bars data controllers from subjecting a data subject to a decision based solely on automated processing with legal effects without consent or a legal basis, and section 10(5)(f) prohibits automated decision-making on children's data that affects children's rights; contraventions are offences punishable by a fine up to level 11 or up to seven years' imprisonment.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding regulation that turns the Act's automated-decision right into a controller obligation backed by criminal penalties and adds a specific ban on automated decisions about children.

instruments.official_title: State of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the Postal & Telecommunications Sector in Zimbabwe
instruments.english_title: State of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the Postal and Telecommunications Sector in Zimbabwe
instruments.issuing_authority: Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority of Zimbabwe (Research & Development Department)
instruments.current_status: Published November 2023 (date on the cover); listed under POTRAZ Studies & Surveys. Research report with recommendations; not binding.
instruments.summary: POTRAZ survey-based assessment of AI adoption by licensed telecommunications operators and postal and courier operators, covering adoption levels, use cases, AI strategies, barriers, skills, investment and regulatory support. It finds low adoption and recommends a multi-stakeholder AI and/or Big Data steering committee, better access to data for AI, a light-touch regulatory framework for responsible AI and a national focus on AI research, innovation and skills.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regulator-published sector AI readiness assessment that informs POTRAZ's regulatory role on AI.
